conviction_note: Mild long lean. Vesta's own run-rate (Q2 ex-energy rental revenue $76.0M, occupancy up 200bp to 91.7% at quarter end) already beats the 10-11% FY2026 guide arithmetically. The reaction history rebuilt from the four confirmed releases is +5.0%, +6.9%, +2.3% and +1.9%, all positive. Against that: the bar is unsourced (one stale aggregator), per-share FFO is diluted by the $270M raise, the stock is +10% in 20 days and 2.6% from its 52-week high, and management may hold any guide change for the 11 November Investor Day. So p_up is only 57 on an abs_move of 3.5. The findings sum to +0.8 and the scaled number is +0.49; the two agree in sign.
bar: Weakly sourced. Q3 2026 revenue consensus is about $78M (range $75-81M, 5 analysts) per TickFlow as of 2026-08-08 (https://tickflow.io/stock/VTMX/forecast); FXEmpire's latest snapshot is Q2 only (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/vtmx/earnings); one EPS figure of $0.30 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/VTMX) is IFRS EPS driven by revaluation gains and is not a usable bar. The company guide is FY2026 rental revenue +10.0-11.0% on 2025's $273.6M, i.e. $301-304M, with Adj. NOI margin ~93.5% and Adj. EBITDA margin ~83% (Q4 2025 release, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260219555425/en/Corporaci%C3%B3n-Inmobiliaria-Vesta-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Earnings-Results). There are not two agreeing estimate sources, so every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: No listed options (baseline: no_options_market), so there is no skew and no implied move. US ADS short interest is 232,016 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement with 3.53 days to cover; it was 226,131 on 09-15 and 259,817 on 07-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/vtmx/shortinterest). That is not crowded: well under 1% of the ADS-equivalent share count. 20-day run-up +9.97%, 5-day +3.4%, 2.61% below the 52-week high; 20-day realised vol 19% annualised; average volume about 64k ADS a day (~$2.3M).

findings.finding: Vesta's H1 2026 ex-energy rental revenue was $150.0M (Q1 $74.0M, Q2 $76.0M). Only $151-154M ($75.5-77M a quarter) is needed in H2 to land inside the FY2026 guide of +10-11% on $273.6M. Q2's run-rate of $76.0M already sits at that level, and total occupancy rose 200bp in Q2 to 91.7% at quarter end, so Q3 ex-energy revenue of about $78-79M would put the year on a ~13-14% track. A raise of the 10-11% guide (or a beat against the ~$78M total-revenue consensus) is the likely line at this print. Precedent: at Q3 2025 Vesta raised its EBITDA-margin guide, and it beat the top of its 2025 revenue guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rebuilt from Yahoo closes on confirmed release dates (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/VTMX?range=1y&interval=1d). Q3 2025 (the EBITDA-margin guide raise, 23 Oct 2025): +4.96%. Q4 2025 (beat the top of the 2025 revenue guide, 19 Feb 2026): +6.89%. Q1 2026: +2.31%. Q2 2026 (guide maintained, Jul 22): +1.93%. The name has paid for beats and guide raises.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Sell-side models probably already sit above a guide that H1 has outrun, and the stock is +10% in 20 days. If the market fully expected a raise, the stock would be expected to be flat on one. The ~$78M aggregator consensus from August is at or below Q2's own $78.5M total revenue, which suggests that at least the stale estimates do not carry the occupancy step-up. A further reason a raise may not come: the 11 Nov Investor Day is where a Route 2030 or guidance update may be held.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001969373/000196937326000013/quarterlyreport1q2026ex-991.htm) gives the $74.0M Q1 ex-energy figure. On the Q2 call the CFO was 'comfortable with the guidance' and expected 'very good results' in H2, with a 'quite strong' pipeline (https://www.webull.com/news/15277439136130048). The Q3 2025 margin-guide raise is in https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251023983156/en/Corporaci%C3%B3n-Inmobiliaria-Vesta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Earnings-Results. All of these are company documents.

findings.finding: FIBRA Prologis, the closest listed Mexico industrial peer, reported Q3 2026 on 21 Oct (after Vesta last spoke). Period-end occupancy rose to 96.5% from 95.8% in Q2, and the CEO cited 'improving customer demand and lower construction starts'. Against that, same-store cash NOI was only +1.7% (vs +14.8% a year ago), retention was 66.0% (vs 81.7%), rollover rent change was 36.2% (vs 47.2%), and average occupancy was 95.1%. The read-through for Vesta's Q3 leasing and occupancy is modestly positive; the read-through on pricing momentum is softer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of how VTMX trades on a peer read-through. Prologis Inc's Q3 call (15 Oct) said Mexico is 'normalizing' with market rents softening but strong mark-to-market (https://bullfincher.io/companies/prologis/earnings-call/fy2026-q3).
findings.why_not_priced: Released yesterday evening, on a BMV-listed FIBRA that US ADS holders of VTMX may not track. The sequential occupancy gain is the forward-relevant part. It is mixed enough (NOI, retention) that the market has no clear signal to trade on.
findings.independence: Prologis Inc Q3 2026 commentary (https://bullfincher.io/companies/prologis/earnings-call/fy2026-q3) is a different document from the same sponsor family. It says Mexico is normalizing, with softer market rents.

findings.finding: CBRE's Q3 2026 Mexico City industrial report (13 Oct) shows 9-month net demand of 875,205 m2 and gross absorption above 1.5M m2, but vacancy is up 2.8pp year on year and 509,690 m2 of new Class A supply arrived in the quarter. Vesta said on its Q2 call that its Mexico City portfolio is 100% occupied, so the direct exposure is to demand, which is strong, rather than to vacancy.
findings.why_not_priced: A market-level proxy in the Spanish trade press. It is mixed, so if anything it is noise to the ADS market; filed small as a proxy.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15277439136130048) says Mexico City is at 100% occupancy and rents have 'not adjusted at all since last year'.

findings.finding: Per-share FFO is diluted. The May-June 2026 equity offering (~$270M gross at $34.62/ADS, ~58M local shares plus ~2M ADSs, roughly 9% more shares) is not yet deployed: cash was $404.2M at 30 June. Q2 Vesta FFO per share fell 1.8% year on year to $0.0493, and after-tax FFO per share fell 26.2% to $0.0324. Q3 carries the first full quarter of the new share count, so FFO per share is likely flat to down year on year even as total FFO grows. The money funds a visible development programme (1.8M sf under construction, 22% pre-leased, 10.1% yield on cost, Monterrey data-centre-equipment leases), so this is a quality point and not a distress one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed the same per-share decline and the stock rose 1.93% the next session, so the market looked through it once.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the dilution has been public since May. What is new is that Q3 is the first full quarter of it while the cash is still largely undeployed. An investor who looks at per-share FFO rather than headline revenue growth will see a weaker number than the 'record revenue' headline.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1 (the Q2 6-K), a different line. The Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15277439136130048) confirms deployment at about $300M a year with no fixed timeline.

findings.finding: The peso is stronger year on year. The Q1 2026 average was 17.568 MXN/USD against 20.422 a year earlier, and Monex's August forecast puts the 2026 average at 17.47 against roughly 18.7 in Q3 2025. About 11% of Vesta's rent is peso-denominated (88.9% USD in Q1), so USD-reported revenue gets a tailwind of about 0.7-1% in Q3. Peso costs rise in USD terms at the same time, which trims the margin effect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 2026 the company quantified the FX translation benefit at about $1.07M (1.6% of revenue). There is no observed reaction to this line by itself.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: FX is public and analysts model it. Filed small because it adds to the revenue beat in finding 1 rather than standing alone.
findings.independence: Monex forecast (https://www.monex.com.mx/portal/download/reportes/260813%20Pronosticos.pdf) is a different source for the 2026 average rate.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: the ADS is +9.97% over 20 sessions and +3.4% over 5 to $35.86, 2.6% under its 52-week high, with no option market to hedge. That leaves sell-the-news room if the print only matches a run-up that already assumed a raise. Short interest is small (232k ADS, 3.5 days to cover), so there is no squeeze fuel either way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two largest confirmed reactions (+4.96% in Oct 2025 at $27.41, +6.89% in Feb 2026) came off lower bases. The Q2 2026 reaction, from $33.66 near the then range, was +1.93%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The run-up is the market's own lean toward a good print, so the finding argues the upside is partly used up rather than that something is unseen.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline tape (run_up_20d_pct 9.97, pct_from_52w_high -2.61) is a different source from the short-interest page.

outside_window.finding: Vesta's 2026 Investor Day in New York on 11 Nov 2026 is set to cover capital allocation, the long-term growth outlook and Route 2030. Any formal multi-year or guidance reset may be held for it, which lowers the odds of a raise at this print.

The USTR public consultation ahead of the 2027 USMCA joint review runs to 12 Jan 2027, with the US on annual reviews after declining the July 2026 extension. This is policy overhang for Mexican industrial demand.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Fitch upgrade of Vesta to 'BBB' stable, and repayment of $105M of private financings (reported 31 Aug 2026)
rejected_candidates.source: search snippet only, no retrievable URL
rejected_candidates.detail: Seen only in a search summary with no URL returned for the Fitch action. It would at most be a small financing positive and is long since public.
The sweep flagged it untrustworthy: a 20-day cadence of 6-K matches. Rebuilt instead from confirmed release dates: +4.96%, +6.89%, +2.31%, +1.93% (Yahoo daily closes).
IFRS EPS is dominated by property revaluation gains (H1 2026 net profit $202.8M vs $42.6M), so this is not a bar the stock trades on. Aggregators also disagree ($0.12 vs $1.25 for Q1).

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The +10% 20-day run-up to near the 52-week high already leans the way the guidance finding points, which is why p_up is only 57 despite a company run-rate above guide and four straight positive reactions.
lessons_applied: Last lesson (rebuild the base rate when baseline_history_trustworthy is false): rebuilt the reaction history from confirmed releases (+4.96, +6.89, +2.31, +1.93). abs_move_pct went up from 2.8 to 3.5 and p_up from 55 to 57, since the name has bought its beats.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the equity raise funds visible development and leasing, so the per-share FFO dilution finding shrank from -0.6 to -0.4.
Rule 5 (proxies small): the FIBRA Prologis read-through went from +0.4 to +0.3 and the CBRE CDMX series from +0.2 to +0.1.

Rule 6 (unsourced bar): the bar has only one stale aggregator, so the guidance finding is held at +1.0 rather than sized up, and print_vs_bar was trimmed from 3.0 to 2.5. Rule 7: with no crowded short and no skew, the positioning negative was trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4.
